Case study / Concept project

BabySteps

An app that helps pregnant women track and manage their pregnancies and health from conception till due date.

Role
Solo UX/UI designer
Platform
Mobile
Timeline
2 weeks
Team
Concept project
The starting point

During my visits to the hospital, I kept seeing heavily pregnant women moving between waiting areas, appointments and different parts of the hospital, often already tired.

It made me think about everything they still had to manage once they left: appointments, changes in the pregnancy, medication, work and their own wellbeing. BabySteps started as an attempt to make some of that easier to manage from a phone.

The turning point

The plan was a pregnancy tracker. The women I spoke to showed me tracking was only part of it.

I spoke to women at the hospital and ran a Google Form survey for mothers and pregnant women. Tracking came up, but so did antenatal appointments, pregnancy-safe medication, fatigue, work and, most of all, mental wellbeing. So the project became about reducing the number of things women had to manage separately.

  1. 01Keep up with datesPregnancy progress, baby development, due dates and appointments all had to be tracked.
  2. 02Get accessible careBooking antenatal visits, finding safe medication or reaching a physician took effort she didn't have.
  3. 03Keep going mentallyAll of it was happening alongside work, everyday life and her own wellbeing.
Research

What I heard, and what already existed.

Survey responses and hospital conversations kept coming back to the same seven problems:

Finding pregnancy-safe medicationBooking antenatal appointmentsFollowing baby's growth accuratelyWork-life balanceLimited choice of physicianFatigue on hospital visitsMental wellbeing

I want to keep track of my baby's growth and my antenatal appointments, but my schedule doesn't leave room for it.Amina, 27. Customer support agent in Ilorin, first pregnancy. The persona I designed for.
The product model

Three jobs, not seven features.

Instead of treating every pain point as its own feature, I grouped the experience around three jobs. It made it much easier to decide where everything belonged.

01

Know

Help her understand where she is in her pregnancy and keep important information close.

Timeline · Due-date calculator · Reminders
02

Care

Reduce the effort of taking the first step towards care.

Clinics · Antenatal booking · Pharmacy
03

Support

Make space for the mental and everyday side of pregnancy too.

Virtual therapy · Prenatal yoga
The product

Inside BabySteps.

Three chapters, one for each job.

01

Know

Pregnancy information changes every week, so BabySteps gives her one place to come back to. Setup takes two answers, and she's placed in her journey straight away.

  • This week, at a glanceBaby's size and how far along she is, in plain words.
  • What's nextThe next appointment sits right under it, one tap from the details.
  • Small daily winsReminders she can tick off without opening anything else.
02

Care

Some problems weren't about information. They were about access. Booking and medication come into the app, so they stop being another trip when she's already tired.

  • Search by drug or symptomIf she only knows how she feels, she can start there.
  • Dose and price on the cardNo second screen needed to decide.
  • Delivered, not another tripThe page says when it arrives. That's the point of a pharmacy in the app.
03

Support

Fatigue and mental wellbeing came up as often as appointments. Therapy and yoga sit on the same shelf as antenatal care, not in a corner of their own.

Structure

Tracking, clinics, pharmacy, therapy and wellbeing, without it feeling like five different apps.

I mapped how the areas connect, then worked the journeys through on paper and in low-fidelity wireframes before the final interface.

Looking back

If I picked it up again today.

  1. 01Validate the main journeys again

    Another round of usability testing on booking, pharmacy and therapy, the most sensitive parts, before expanding them.

  2. 02Work out who else belongs

    Fathers and partners were on my list. I'd find out what they actually need first, and whether it belongs in BabySteps at all.

  3. 03Expand only where research supports it

    Pregnancy touches so much of life that BabySteps could get overwhelming if every problem became a feature.

The lesson

Don't get attached to the first version of an idea. A tracker became an attempt to make the everyday work of pregnancy lighter.
